{{italic title}}

'''''A Treatise on the Circle and the Sphere''''' is a mathematics book on [[circle]]s, [[sphere]]s, and [[inversive geometry]]. It was written by [[Julian Coolidge]] and published by the [[Clarendon Press]] in 1916.{{r|bieberbach|hph|emch|white}} The [[Chelsea Publishing Company]] published a corrected reprint in 1971.{{r|mr71|peak}} After the [[American Mathematical Society]] acquired Chelsea Publishing it was reprinted again in 1997.{{r|steinke}}

==Topics==
As is now standard in inversive geometry, the book extends the [[Euclidean plane]] to its [[Alexandroff extension|one-point compactification]], and considers Euclidean lines to be a degenerate case of circles, passing through the [[point at infinity]]. It identifies every circle with the inversion through it, and studies circle inversions as a [[Group (mathematics)|group]], the group of [[Möbius transformation]]s of the extended plane. Another key tool used by the book are the "tetracyclic coordinates" of a circle, quadruples of complex numbers <math>a, b, c, d</math> describing the circle in the [[complex plane]] as the solutions to the equation <math>az\bar z+bz+c\bar z+d=0</math>. It applies similar methods in three dimensions to identify spheres (and planes as degenerate spheres) with the inversions through them, and to coordinatize spheres by "pentacyclic coordinates".{{r|steinke}}

Other topics described in the book include:
*[[Tangent circles]]{{r|hph|emch}} and [[Apollonian circles|pencils of circles]]{{r|emch}}
*[[Steiner chain]]s, rings of circles tangent to two given circles{{r|white}}
*[[Ptolemy's theorem]] on the sides and diagonals of quadrilaterals inscribed in circles{{r|white}}
*Triangle geometry, and circles associated with triangles, including the [[nine-point circle]], [[Brocard circle]], and [[Lemoine hexagon|Lemoine circle]]{{r|bieberbach|hph|emch}}
*The [[Problem of Apollonius]] on constructing a circle tangent to three given circles, and the [[Malfatti circles|Malfatti problem]] of constructing three mutually-tangent circles, each tangent to two sides of a given triangle{{r|bieberbach|emch}}
*The work of [[Wilhelm Fiedler]] on "cyclography", constructions involving circles and spheres{{r|bieberbach|emch}}
*The [[Mohr–Mascheroni theorem]], that in [[straightedge and compass construction]]s, it is possible to use only the compass{{r|bieberbach}}
*[[Laguerre transformations]], analogues of Möbius transformations for [[oriented projective geometry]]{{r|bieberbach|emch}}
*[[Dupin cyclide]]s, shapes obtained from cylinders and tori by inversion{{r|emch}}

==Legacy==
At the time of its original publication this book was called encyclopedic,{{r|hph|emch}} and "likely to become and remain the standard for a long period".{{r|hph}} It has since been called a classic,{{r|mr71|steinke}} in part because of its unification of aspects of the subject previously studied separately in [[synthetic geometry]], [[analytic geometry]], [[projective geometry]], and [[differential geometry]].{{r|mr71}} At the time of its 1971 reprint, it was still considered "one of the most complete publications on the circle and the sphere", and "an excellent reference".{{r|peak}}
